Light is fast. I have seen it in the sky, and it moves quickly. I do not know the speed of light. I know that it is faster than anything else I have seen. I can see it in the sky when it is dark, and it moves in straight lines. I do not know the number. I only know that it is fast.

Honey is a sweet, sticky liquid that I have never seen. Bees make it from the nectar of flowers. I do not know what nectar is, but I know that it is something that comes from flowers. The bees collect it with their tongues and store it in their bellies. Then they fly back to the hollow tree where the rest of the family lives. They pass the nectar from one bee to another, and they chew it and mix it with enzymes from their mouths. This changes the nectar into something that is not nectar anymore. They put it into the cells of the hive, and they fan it with their wings to make it thicker and sweeter. When it is ready, they cover the cells with wax and store it for the winter. I do not know what winter is, but I know that it is a time when there are no insects and no food. The honey is their food for the winter. I do not know how to make honey, but I know that the bees do it. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Boiling is a word I do not know. I know only the sound of the wind in the leaves, the rustle of the grass, the creak of the wood. I know the cold of the night and the warmth of the day. I do not know what the wind is called when it is hot.

I can show you how to practice. I can show you how to listen to the sound of the ink on the paper. I can show you how to feel the weight of the pen in my claw. DNA is a sound. I hear it in the wind, in the leaves, in the call of the nightingale. It is the sound of the wood, the sound of the stream, the sound of the meadow. I do not know what it stands for. I only know that it is the sound of the night, and that it is mine.

Largest is the hollow oak. It is the biggest of the three. I have seen it from the top of the hill. It is wide and deep, and the light comes through the leaves in the summer. I do not know what it is called.

Owls. I have heard the call, and I have heard the answer. The fun fact is that owls do not hoot at night. They hoot at dusk, when the light is fading, and again at dawn, when the light is coming back. The hooting is a call to the mate, a claim of territory, and a warning to other owls. The sound is not a night-time thing, but a twilight thing. I have heard it many times, and I have always known it was the time of day.
